html:
The amphitheatre of El Jem is a vast Roman arena in central Tunisia, built around 238 CE in the town of Thysdrus. It held some 35,000 people and is one of the largest amphitheatres outside Italy.

Thysdrus was rich from the olive oil of the region. In 238 a revolt there proclaimed the local governor Gordian as emperor, a short-lived bid for power. The arena was built about that time and may never have been finished.

Later it served as a fortress. By tradition the Berber queen al-Kahina made a stand there against the Arabs around 700. It became a World Heritage Site in 1979. Compare the Roman ruins of Timgad in Algeria.
